summary: Sheldon Pollock is an Indologist and linguist who studied under Daniel H. H. Ingalls. He held professorships at the University of Iowa, the University of Chicago (1990), and Columbia University (circa 2005–2023), where he became Professor Emeritus.

Sheng Yen was a Buddhist and religious studies scholar who earned doctorates at Rissho University and studied under Dongchu and Lingyuan. He founded the Chung-Hwa Institute of Buddhist Studies, serving on its faculty from circa 1985 to 2009.

Shenghai Li is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who completed his Ph.D. at the University of Wisconsin-Madison (2004–2012) under Donald R. Davis Jr. He held fellowships at Harvard University (2013–2015) and Hebrew University of Jerusalem (2015–2016).

Shenpen Hookham is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. She studied at the University of Reading and completed a D.Phil. at the University of Oxford (circa 1980–1986) supervised by Michael M. Broido.

Shenphen Nangwa (1871–1927) was a scholar in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy. He studied under Patrul Rinpoche and Önpo Tenzin Norbu, taught at Dzogchen Monastery (1902), and founded Dzongsar Monastery, becoming the first khenpo of its shedra (1918).

Sherab Chomphel is a scholar of Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy. He earned a B.A. from the College for Higher Tibetan Studies (2012–2015), an M.A. from Banaras Hindu University (2016–2018), and pursued an MTS at Harvard University (2022–2025).

Sherab Gyatso was a scholar in Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy who studied at Labrang and Drepung Monasteries. He founded the Buddhist Association of China in 1952, served as its president (circa 1953–1966), and was Dean at the Buddhist Academy of China.

Sherry B. Ortner is a scholar of Tibetology and religious studies. She studied at Bryn Mawr College and the University of Chicago, and held posts at Sarah Lawrence College, the University of Michigan, and the University of California, Los Angeles.
Sherry Chayat is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Vassar College and under Eido Shimano circa 1967.
Shesh Dev Pandey is an Indologist who completed his Shastri degree at Banaras Hindu University between 2020 and 2023.

Shi Hu was a scholar of philosophy, sinology, and history and archaeology. He earned his PhD at Columbia University under John Dewey, taught at Peking University (circa 1917–1948), and served as president of Academia Sinica (1958–1962).

Shi Wang works in history and archaeology, Buddhist studies, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. Wang earned a BA at Yale University (2020–2024) and studied for a DPhil at the University of Oxford (2024–2025).

Shichang Ma was a history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies scholar. He worked as a Buddhist archaeology researcher at Dunhuang Academy (1963–1978) and served in the Archaeology Department at Peking University beginning in 1982.
Shigeki Kaizuka was a scholar of sinology and history and archaeology. He studied at Kyoto University from circa 1925 to 1928 and later served on its faculty from circa 1949 to 1968.
Shigeki Kudo is a Buddhist studies scholar who held academic posts at Kyoto University, Shuchiin University, and Shitennoji University (attested 1972–1973).

Shigeki Moro is a scholar of Buddhist studies, computational fields, and philosophy. He earned degrees at Waseda, Toyo, and Kansai universities, and served as a professor at Hanazono University (2002–2025) before joining Waseda University as professor in 2025.
Shigemasa Fukui is a sinologist and historian. He studied at Waseda University from circa 1954 to 1963 and later served there as a professor from circa 1978 to 2006.

Shigemitsu Dando studied under Seiichiro Ono at the University of Tokyo (circa 1932–1935). He held faculty posts at the University of Tokyo and Keio University, and served on the Supreme Court of Japan from circa 1974 to 1983.
Shigenori Nagatomo is a scholar in religious studies, philosophy, and Buddhist studies who served as a professor of religious studies at Temple University (attested 1999 and 2017).

Shigeo Kamata was a scholar of Buddhist studies and sinology who earned his doctorate from the University of Tokyo. He held posts at the University of Tokyo, the Institute for Advanced Studies on Asia, and Aichi Gakuin University (circa 1988–1996).
